title: "Solution: Decision Trees and Random Forests"

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
library(pROC)

options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")
health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 50000, seed = 602)
```

```{r split-data}
set.seed(602)
idx   <- sample(nrow(health_data), 0.80 * nrow(health_data))
train <- health_data[idx, ]
test  <- health_data[-idx, ]

train$churned <- factor(train$churned, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
test$churned  <- factor(test$churned,  levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
```

## Task 1: Train and plot a decision tree

```{r task1-tree}
tree <- rpart(
  churned ~ age + plan_tier + income + num_claims + support_calls +
            auto_pay + customer_rating + deductible,
  data   = train,
  method = "class",
  cp     = 0.005
)
rpart.plot(tree, type = 4, extra = 104, main = "Decision Tree — Churn Prediction")
```

```{r task1-tree-summary}
printcp(tree)
```

## Task 2: Tune cp with plotcp()

```{r task2-plotcp}
plotcp(tree)
```

```{r task2-prune}
best_cp <- tree$cptable[which.min(tree$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"]
cat("Best cp:", best_cp, "\n")

tree_pruned <- prune(tree, cp = best_cp)
rpart.plot(tree_pruned, type = 4, extra = 104, main = "Pruned Decision Tree — Churn")
```

## Task 3: Train a random forest and plot variable importance

```{r task3-rf}
set.seed(602)
rf <- randomForest(
  churned ~ age + plan_tier + income + num_claims + support_calls +
            auto_pay + customer_rating + deductible,
  data       = train,
  ntree      = 200,
  mtry       = floor(sqrt(8)),
  importance = TRUE
)
print(rf)
```

```{r task3-varimp}
varImpPlot(rf, main = "Random Forest Variable Importance — Churn")
```

```{r task3-top-vars}
# Top 3 variables by Mean Decrease in Gini (typical results):
# 1. customer_rating — directly captures dissatisfaction, the strongest churn signal
# 2. support_calls   — frequent complaints predict churn
# 3. auto_pay        — customers on auto-pay are less likely to churn (negative predictor)
# These make business sense: unhappy customers who call often and don't autopay are most at risk.
```

## Task 4: Compare decision tree vs. random forest

```{r task4-predictions}
prob_tree <- predict(tree_pruned, test, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
prob_rf   <- predict(rf, test, type = "prob")[, "Yes"]
```

```{r task4-roc}
roc_tree <- roc(test$churned, prob_tree, levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)
roc_rf   <- roc(test$churned, prob_rf,   levels = c("No", "Yes"), quiet = TRUE)

plot(roc_tree, col = "steelblue", main = "ROC Curves: Decision Tree vs. Random Forest")
lines(roc_rf, col = "darkorange")
legend("bottomright", legend = c(
  paste("Decision Tree AUC =", round(auc(roc_tree), 3)),
  paste("Random Forest AUC =", round(auc(roc_rf),   3))
), col = c("steelblue", "darkorange"), lwd = 2)
```

```{r task4-f1}
compute_f1 <- function(prob, truth, threshold = 0.5) {
  pred <- factor(ifelse(prob > threshold, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
  cm   <- table(Predicted = pred, Actual = truth)
  TP   <- cm["Yes", "Yes"]
  FP   <- cm["Yes", "No"]
  FN   <- cm["No",  "Yes"]
  P    <- TP / (TP + FP)
  R    <- TP / (TP + FN)
  2 * P * R / (P + R)
}

f1_tree <- compute_f1(prob_tree, test$churned)
f1_rf   <- compute_f1(prob_rf,   test$churned)

cat("Decision Tree F1:", round(f1_tree, 3), "\n")
cat("Random Forest F1:", round(f1_rf,   3), "\n")

# Random forest wins on both AUC and F1.
# The ensemble of 200 decorrelated trees produces smoother probability estimates
# and is less sensitive to the specific training sample than a single tree.
```
